text:
Open with the task: mapping green-roof area at pixel level from aerial imagery. The study is deliberately restricted to Berlin postcode 12357 so that the first experiment is small, reproducible, and spatially auditable.

Define the task as semantic segmentation: every pixel receives a green-roof or background label. The imbalance exists at two levels—only 182 of 1,635 tiles are positive, and only 0.6001% of all pixels are foreground.

text:
The proposal is not another architecture race. The methodological gap is whether the complete workflow yields credible spatial evidence. Spatially structured data violate the independence assumption of ordinary random cross-validation; block-based evaluation is therefore the safer baseline.

U-Net is chosen because its encoder–decoder structure and skip connections offer a clear baseline for pixel localization. ResNet50 supplies pretrained visual features. DeepLabv3+ and SegFormer remain suitable follow-up baselines once the data and evaluation protocol are stable.

text:
Walk left to right. XYZ already defines the image grid. Mercantile gives each tile's Web Mercator bounds. Green-roof polygons are loaded, validated and transformed to EPSG:3857. Shapely selects intersections; Rasterio maps the intersecting geometry into the exact 256 by 256 mask.

text:
First the current official postcode boundary selects tiles by centre point. Then 8 by 8 tile blocks—not individual tiles—are assigned to train, validation and test. The diagnostic shows a 47 m median nearest-neighbour distance within training and 93 m from held-out tiles to training. This is a proxy for spatial separation, not a guarantee of city-wide deployment performance.

The dataset contains 1,635 tiles. Only 182 are positive and 1,453 contain no green-roof pixels. Across all tiles, only 643,038 of 107,151,360 pixels are foreground. Accuracy would therefore be misleading; Dice, IoU, precision, recall and negative-scene false positives are used instead.

This is a controlled ablation. Both runs see 1,180 samples per epoch, identical validation images and the same synchronized flips and 90-degree rotations. The all-tile strategy balances 590 positive with 590 negative scenes; positive-only repeats positive examples to match the optimizer-step budget.

text:
The pixel totals alone would hide the deployment risk. Positive-only training produces slightly fewer false-positive pixels, but at least one false positive appears in 65 of 181 negative validation tiles, compared with 10 of 181 for all-tile training. In area-wide mapping, spatial spread of false alarms matters.

The current training augmentation is deliberately simple and label-safe: independent 50% horizontal and vertical flips plus a random right-angle rotation. The image and mask always receive the same transform. Validation is deterministic.
